title: Dermatology Language Access: A Clinical Workflow
summary: Build a dermatology language access workflow for skin exams, topical medications, biopsies, results, wound care, and teledermatology.
body_markdown:
###


Collect the patient’s preferred spoken and written languages, dialect when relevant, safe contact method, interpreter preference, and any preparation needs. Ask the patient to bring medication containers, skin products, or prior records when clinically relevant.


###


Connect each product to its amount, exact body site, frequency, duration, areas to avoid, expected response, and stop or call conditions. Ask the patient to explain or demonstrate the plan.


###


Interpret the reason for the biopsy, what the procedure involves, expected discomfort, risks, alternatives when relevant, aftercare, and the result process. Keep a suspected diagnosis separate from the pathology result.


###


Ask the patient to show where a medicine goes, describe wound care in order, name warning signs, and explain how results will arrive. Rephrase and recheck any part that remains unclear.


###


Yes, when the workflow includes privacy controls, clear audio, body-site confirmation, verification of medication details, teach-back, documentation, and another option when patient preference, policy, or encounter needs call for it.
